subject: subj:physio

Keeps free glucose low and traps it inside

title: Optimal BMI for most people is:

body.stem: Optimal BMI for most people is:

title: How many axons does a neuron have?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many axons does a neuron have?
body.explanation: All neurons contain one and only one axon; dendrites may be absent, one or many.

title: The macula densa cells are:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The macula densa cells are:
options: Chemoreceptors for NaCl in the filtrate

title: Which help maintain arterial pH?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which help maintain arterial pH?

title: Why do marathon runners sometimes have proteinuria?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why do marathon runners sometimes have proteinuria?
body.explanation: Prolonged strenuous exercise reduces renal perfusion, and the glomerulus deteriorates under prolonged hypoxia, allowing temporary proteinuria or haematuria.

title: What is the normal resting sarcomere length?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the normal resting sarcomere length?
body.explanation: Optimal overlap of thick and thin filaments gives the greatest tension; too much or too little reduces it.

title: How much filtrate is formed per day?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How much filtrate is formed per day?
body.explanation: About 2 mL per second, 120 per minute, some 170 to 180 L per day: 50 to 60 times the blood volume.

title: PCTs alone use about what share of resting ATP?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: PCTs alone use about what share of resting ATP?
body.explanation: PCTs account for about 6% of resting ATP and calorie consumption.

title: What is eustress?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is eustress?
body.explanation: Eustress enhances function; distress is persistent and unresolved by coping or adaptation.

title: Adenosine in tubuloglomerular feedback causes:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Adenosine in tubuloglomerular feedback causes:
body.explanation: Adenosine stimulates granular cells, which constrict the afferent arteriole; GFR falls back.

title: Fat's glucose-sparing effect keeps glucose for:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Fat's glucose-sparing effect keeps glucose for:
body.explanation: Glucose is spared for cells that cannot use fat, such as neurons.

title: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the inhibitory interneuron. The fully labelled arc is on the Visual tab.

title: Insulin's effect on leptin secretion from adipose tissue is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Insulin's effect on leptin secretion from adipose tissue is:
body.explanation: Insulin stimulates leptin secretion.

title: Stimulus intensity is coded by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Stimulus intensity is coded by:
options: Larger action potential amplitude in the afferent
Number of receptors and action potential frequency
Which ion carries the receptor potential
Faster conduction velocity of the afferent axon
body.explanation: Action potentials are all-or-none.

title: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the alpha motor neuron (to quadriceps). The fully labelled arc is on the Visual tab.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the grey matter (butterfly).

title: Which neurons have long axons reaching remote organs?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which neurons have long axons reaching remote organs?
body.explanation: Golgi type I neurons have long axons from the CNS to remote organs; Golgi type II have short axons in the cortex and cord.

title: Which element is at the arrow?

body.explanation: The arrow points to: Thick filament. About 250 myosin II molecules; about 16 nm wide.

title: A BMI of 32 is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A BMI of 32 is:
body.explanation: Above 30: obese.

title: Which nerve carries the motor arm of the corneal reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which nerve carries the motor arm of the corneal reflex?
body.explanation: Touch is sensed by the trigeminal nerve; its sensory nucleus synapses on the facial motor nucleus, which closes the eye and drives lacrimation.

title: Which channel mediates sour taste?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which channel mediates sour taste?
body.explanation: Sour taste comes from H+ entering through the proton channel PKD2L1, a TRP-type channel.

title: Which arteriole is larger?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which arteriole is larger?
body.explanation: The afferent arteriole is larger than the efferent arteriole.

title: Rigor mortis is caused by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Rigor mortis is caused by:
body.explanation: Without ATP myosin cannot detach from actin.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Renin. Released by the granular (juxtaglomerular) cells, triggered by sympathetic fibres.

title: With maximal ADH, urine output is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: With maximal ADH, urine output is about:
body.explanation: Max ADH: 119.75 mL/min reabsorbed; urine 0.25 mL/min ≈ 375 mL/day.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Presynaptic action potential. Arrives at the axon terminal purely by electrical conduction along the axon.

title: The only way to eliminate acids other than carbonic acid is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The only way to eliminate acids other than carbonic acid is:
body.explanation: Only the kidneys eliminate non-volatile acids.

title: Which spindle endings signal only static limb position (length), not the velocity of movement?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which spindle endings signal only static limb position (length), not the velocity of movement?
body.explanation: Secondary (group II) endings, mainly on nuclear chain fibres, signal length only, i.e. static position. Primary (Ia) endings signal both length and the velocity and direction of movement.
option_notes: Correct: group II endings signal length only (static position).
Ia endings signal length and speed, so they are not static-only.
Golgi tendon organs signal tension, not length (group Ib).
Free nerve endings are mainly nociceptors and thermoreceptors.

title: What gel covers the hair cells of the canals?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What gel covers the hair cells of the canals?
body.explanation: Cupula in the canals; otolithic membrane in the utricle and saccule.

title: What happens during steady head rotation?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What happens during steady head rotation?
body.explanation: At constant velocity friction brings the endolymph to the same speed, so the cupula and receptors return to rest.

title: Leptin levels are proportional to:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Leptin levels are proportional to:
body.explanation: Leptin informs the brain how much fat we have.

title: Which hormone stimulates NPY and AgRP secretion?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which hormone stimulates NPY and AgRP secretion?
body.explanation: Ghrelin stimulates; insulin, PYY, CCK and leptin inhibit.

title: The basal Na+–K+ pump is an example of:

body.stem: The basal Na+–K+ pump is an example of:
body.explanation: It uses ATP directly: primary active transport.

title: Which order is correct for the HPA axis?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which order is correct for the HPA axis?
body.explanation: Your professor's question: hypothalamus CRH, anterior pituitary ACTH, adrenal cortex cortisol.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Oxygen. Final electron acceptor; each O atom takes 2 electrons and 2 protons to form metabolic water.

title: Lipoproteins are produced by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Lipoproteins are produced by:
body.explanation: Lipoproteins are produced in the liver (chylomicrons in the intestine).

title: Digoxin inhibits:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Digoxin inhibits:
body.explanation: Digoxin (from Digitalis lanata) blocks the Na+/K+-ATPase.

title: What is the main inhibitor of CRH and ACTH release?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the main inhibitor of CRH and ACTH release?
body.explanation: Cortisol feeds back to inhibit CRH and ACTH secretion by regulating gene expression.

title: How many twitches can stored sarcoplasmic ATP power?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many twitches can stored sarcoplasmic ATP power?
body.explanation: The sarcoplasm holds enough ATP for about 8 twitches; creatine kinase keeps ADP/ATP low for continuous work.

title: What is treppe?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is treppe?
body.explanation: In a muscle rested for a long time, each contraction is stronger than the one before until they level off.

title: How does afferent arteriole constriction affect GFR?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How does afferent arteriole constriction affect GFR?
body.explanation: Less blood enters the glomerulus, so glomerular pressure and GFR fall.

title: Which substances enhance pain endings without exciting them?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which substances enhance pain endings without exciting them?
body.explanation: Bradykinin, serotonin, histamine, K+, acids, ACh and proteolytic enzymes excite pain endings; prostaglandins and substance P only sensitise them.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the white matter (funiculi).

title: What is depolarization?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is depolarization?
body.explanation: Depolarization: less negative, as when positive ions enter. Hyperpolarization: more negative. Repolarization: return to rest.

title: The resting membrane potential in the slides is about:

title: Physiological nephron loss after age 30 is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Physiological nephron loss after age 30 is about:

title: Why does the basement membrane repel albumin?

body.stem: Why does the basement membrane repel albumin?
body.explanation: The proteoglycan gel is negatively charged, repelling negatively charged albumin, and excludes molecules above 8 nm.

title: How many US adults report total loss of smell?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many US adults report total loss of smell?
body.explanation: 1 to 2 percent report total loss of smell; 7 million have taste and 14 million smell disorders.

title: Which division is called the brain of the gut?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which division is called the brain of the gut?
body.explanation: The PNS has three parts: somatic (voluntary), autonomic (involuntary) and enteric (the brain of the gut).

title: Which fibres resist fatigue the most?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which fibres resist fatigue the most?
body.explanation: Type I: slow oxidative, high mitochondria and myoglobin, used for hours. IIa intermediate (under 30 minutes). IIb fast glycolytic, fatigue in under 5 minutes.

title: Cholesterol is a precursor of:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Cholesterol is a precursor of:
body.explanation: Cholesterol → steroid hormones and vitamin D; fatty acids → eicosanoids.

title: Which disease causes an abnormal appetite for salt?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which disease causes an abnormal appetite for salt?

body.explanation: The arrow points to: Angiotensin I. Renin converts angiotensinogen, a blood protein from the liver, into angiotensin I.

title: Insulin promotes:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Insulin promotes:
body.explanation: Insulin promotes glycogen and fat synthesis and inhibits fat breakdown.

title: Which buffer the urine so more H+ can be secreted?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which buffer the urine so more H+ can be secreted?

title: How much protein is in the filtrate compared with plasma?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How much protein is in the filtrate compared with plasma?
body.explanation: Plasma is about 7 percent protein; the filtrate only 0.03 percent.

title: If arterial pressure rises, the afferent arteriole:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: If arterial pressure rises, the afferent arteriole:
body.explanation: It is stretched and constricts, so glomerular flow does not change.

title: Which tract links vestibular nuclei to eye muscle nuclei?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which tract links vestibular nuclei to eye muscle nuclei?
body.explanation: The MLF connects the vestibular nuclei with the oculomotor, trochlear and abducens nuclei and upper spinal motor neurons.

title: Which lipoprotein is about 90% triglyceride?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which lipoprotein is about 90% triglyceride?

title: Which element is at the arrow?

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?

title: What final event triggers transmitter release in taste cells?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What final event triggers transmitter release in taste cells?
body.explanation: All taste responses end in Ca2+ influx, vesicle fusion and neurotransmitter release.

title: What is ageusia?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is ageusia?
body.explanation: Ageusia is loss of taste, not to be confused with anosmia, loss of smell.

title: Which are layers of the glomerular filtration barrier?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are layers of the glomerular filtration barrier?
body.explanation: The barrier has three layers: fenestrated endothelium, basement membrane and the filtration slits between podocyte pedicels.

Negatively charged proteoglycan gel; repels albumin, excludes molecules over 8 nm.
Slits between podocyte foot processes; the last layer before the capsular space.
The fibrous capsule around the kidney; not part of the filtration barrier.

title: Net ATP gain from glycolysis per glucose is:
subject: subj:physio

title: Uric acid comes from the catabolism of:

body.stem: Uric acid comes from the catabolism of:

Descending limb of the loop of Henle

subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?

title: Where are the cytochromes of the electron transport chain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where are the cytochromes of the electron transport chain?
body.explanation: Embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane (cristae).

title: Which disease smells like decomposing apples?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which disease smells like decomposing apples?
body.explanation: Diabetic ketosis: fruity; typhoid: baked bread; yellow fever: a butcher's shop; scrofula: stale beer; diphtheria: sweet.

title: Renal autoregulation works:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Renal autoregulation works:
options: Without external nervous or hormonal control
body.explanation: It is the nephrons' ability to adjust their own flow and GFR without external control.

subject: subj:physio

title: Which two factors increase conduction velocity?
subject: subj:physio

title: In severe anaemia, kidney EPO production can rise:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In severe anaemia, kidney EPO production can rise:
body.explanation: Under hypoxic conditions, EPO can rise more than 100-fold over normal.

title: Why is the resting potential close to the K+ equilibrium?
subject: subj:physio

body.explanation: At rest K+ permeability is high through leak channels, while few Na+ channels are open, so the potential sits near the K+ equilibrium.

title: By how much can SR Ca2+ exceed cytosolic Ca2+?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: By how much can SR Ca2+ exceed cytosolic Ca2+?
body.explanation: Resting cytosol holds about 0.1 µmol/L; the SR may hold 10,000 times more. On release, cytosolic Ca2+ rises 10-fold or more.

title: Where does the Krebs cycle take place?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where does the Krebs cycle take place?
body.explanation: Krebs: matrix. Glycolysis: cytoplasm. ETC: inner membrane.

title: How much does CSF buoyancy reduce the brain's net weight?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How much does CSF buoyancy reduce the brain's net weight?
body.explanation: Buoyancy cuts the net weight from about 1400 g to about 50 g, reducing pressure at the base of the brain.

title: The lowest urine pH the nephron can produce is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The lowest urine pH the nephron can produce is about:
body.explanation: Nephrons cannot produce urine with a pH below 4.5.

title: When GFR is high, macula densa cells secrete:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: When GFR is high, macula densa cells secrete:
body.explanation: They secrete ATP, which mesangial cells metabolise into adenosine.

title: What is hydrocephalus?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is hydrocephalus?
body.explanation: It raises intracranial pressure; in childhood it can enlarge the head and cause convulsions, tunnel vision and mental disability.

title: Which organs detect linear acceleration?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which organs detect linear acceleration?
body.explanation: The otolithic organs detect gravity and linear acceleration, plus pitch and roll tilts. The canals detect angular acceleration.

title: Tetanus toxin causes spasms by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Tetanus toxin causes spasms by:
options: Blocking nicotinic ACh receptors at the end plate
Preventing GABA release from inhibitory neurons
Increasing acetylcholinesterase activity in the cleft
Blocking voltage-gated K⁺ channels in motor axons
body.explanation: Loss of inhibition.

title: In which lamina do A-delta fast pain fibres mainly end?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In which lamina do A-delta fast pain fibres mainly end?

title: Why does an action potential travel only one way along the axon?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why does an action potential travel only one way along the axon?
options: The axon is one-way by structure
body.explanation: The Na+ channels just behind the wave are temporarily inactivated, like dominoes that have already fallen.

title: What fraction of paleospinothalamic fibres reaches the thalamus?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What fraction of paleospinothalamic fibres reaches the thalamus?

title: The DHP receptor is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The DHP receptor is:
options: A Ca²⁺ pump in the SR membrane
A voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channel in the T-tubule
The nicotinic ACh receptor of the end plate
A K⁺ leak channel of the sarcolemma
body.explanation: It gates the ryanodine receptor.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

title: An ob gene mutation causes:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: An ob gene mutation causes:
options: No leptin, no satiety, constant hunger
body.explanation: No leptin → no satiety → always hungry.

title: Which brainstem nucleus is the noradrenaline system?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which brainstem nucleus is the noradrenaline system?

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Catabolism. Breaks large molecules into smaller ones; releases more energy than it uses (exergonic, exothermic).

title: What do the sympathetic fibres to sweat glands release?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do the sympathetic fibres to sweat glands release?

title: Through which opening does CSF pass from the lateral to the third ventricle?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Through which opening does CSF pass from the lateral to the third ventricle?

title: What do neonate taste tests show?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do neonate taste tests show?

title: Who isolated the catalytic F1 subunit of ATP synthase (1961)?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Who isolated the catalytic F1 subunit of ATP synthase (1961)?

title: What happens if GFR is too low?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What happens if GFR is too low?

title: Which division of the vestibular nerve supplies the posterior crista?

body.stem: Which division of the vestibular nerve supplies the posterior crista?

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the anterior (ventral) horn: motor.

title: Where does the slow paleospinothalamic pathway mainly end? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where does the slow paleospinothalamic pathway mainly end? (choose all)

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the saccule.

title: Where does the vestibular nerve enter the brainstem?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where does the vestibular nerve enter the brainstem?
body.explanation: It enters at the cerebellopontine angle and ends in the vestibular nuclear complex.

title: How long does acute stress last?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How long does acute stress last?
body.explanation: Acute stressors are recent and short (under 2 days to 4 weeks); chronic stress lasts longer than a month.

title: Which property describes recoil to resting length?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which property describes recoil to resting length?

title: What type of receptor is the nicotinic ACh receptor?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What type of receptor is the nicotinic ACh receptor?
body.explanation: A ligand-gated, cation-selective channel. Two ACh molecules bind the two α subunits to open it.

title: What do gamma motor neurons do?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do gamma motor neurons do?
body.explanation: They contract the ends of intrafusal fibres, adjusting spindle length to muscle length so the spindle stays sensitive during contraction.

title: Which are cortical vestibular areas? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are cortical vestibular areas? (choose all)
body.explanation: Area 2v, area 3a, area 7 and the parieto-insular vestibular cortex.

title: What share of weight variation is hereditary?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What share of weight variation is hereditary?
body.explanation: 30 to 50% hereditary; environment 50 to 70%.

title: Which are signs of Duchenne muscular dystrophy? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are signs of Duchenne muscular dystrophy? (choose all)
body.explanation: Falls, a waddling gait, using the arms to stand, proximal weakness and calf hypertrophy in a young boy.

title: Starch, cellulose and glycogen are all polymers of:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Starch, cellulose and glycogen are all polymers of:
body.explanation: All three are glucose polymers.

title: What is allodynia?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is allodynia?
options: Pain felt in a lost limb
body.explanation: Allodynia: pain from a normally harmless stimulus, such as light touch on sunburned skin. Hyperalgesia: an exaggerated response to a noxious stimulus.

title: How many synapses are in the CNS part of the myotatic reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many synapses are in the CNS part of the myotatic reflex?
body.explanation: It is monosynaptic: one synapse in the CNS, between the sensory and motor neuron. Counting the neuromuscular junction, the arc has two synapses.

title: Anabolic reactions:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Anabolic reactions:
options: Break large molecules into small ones
Consume more energy than they produce
body.explanation: Anabolism builds molecules and is endergonic, endothermic.

title: What is the power of a lens with a 50 cm focal length?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the power of a lens with a 50 cm focal length?
body.explanation: Refractive power is the inverse of focal length in metres: 1 / 0.5 = 2 D. Convex lenses are positive, concave negative.

title: Tubuloglomerular feedback is an example of:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Tubuloglomerular feedback is an example of:
body.explanation: Negative feedback control of GFR.

title: Where are Nissl granules absent?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where are Nissl granules absent?
body.explanation: Nissl granules, the tigroid substance, are in the cell body and dendrites but absent from the axon and axon hillock.

title: What transmitter do A-delta pain fibres release?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What transmitter do A-delta pain fibres release?
body.explanation: A-delta endings release glutamate, acting for milliseconds. C fibres release glutamate and substance P, which builds up over seconds to minutes.

title: What is the typical net filtration pressure?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the typical net filtration pressure?
body.explanation: Textbook values: glomerular hydrostatic about 60, capsular about 18, colloid osmotic about 32 mmHg, giving about 10 mmHg.

title: During starvation, the kidneys can synthesise glucose from:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: During starvation, the kidneys can synthesise glucose from:
body.explanation: In starvation, the kidneys perform gluconeogenesis from amino acids.

title: What share of the body's serotonin comes from the gut?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What share of the body's serotonin comes from the gut?
body.explanation: Gut mucosal cells and ENS neurons produce 95 percent of the body's serotonin.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Isosmotic filtrate. Fluid entering the loop is isosmotic (about 300 mOsm) with the interstitial fluid.

title: What gastrointestinal effect does chronic stress have?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What gastrointestinal effect does chronic stress have?
body.explanation: Chronic stress causes gastric acid and pepsin hypersecretion, leading to peptic ulcer disease and GERD.

title: Which are polysynaptic reflexes? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are polysynaptic reflexes? (choose all)
body.explanation: The Golgi tendon organ reflex, the flexor (withdrawal) reflex and the crossed extensor reflex are polysynaptic. The myotatic (stretch) reflex, such as the patellar knee jerk, is monosynaptic.
option_notes: Polysynaptic: Ib afferents act through interneurons; the muscle relaxes and the antagonist contracts.
Polysynaptic: interneurons cross the cord so the opposite leg extends to bear weight.
Monosynaptic: Ia afferent synapses directly on the alpha motor neuron.
Monosynaptic: it is a myotatic (deep tendon) reflex, centre L2 to L4.

title: Which phase of the stress response is fast?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which phase of the stress response is fast?
body.explanation: First phase: autonomic (SN and SAM), rapid. Second phase: the HPA axis, sluggish but amplified and protracted.

title: Which vitamins are absorbed with dietary fat?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which vitamins are absorbed with dietary fat?
body.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K.

title: In lactose intolerance the symptoms come from:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In lactose intolerance the symptoms come from:
options: Too much lactase in the small intestine
Bacterial fermentation of lactose in the colon
Lactose absorbed whole into the blood
Excess galactose made by the liver
body.explanation: Undigested lactose is fermented by colonic bacteria into gas and acids.

title: What is miosis?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is miosis?
body.explanation: Miosis is constriction; mydriasis is dilation.

title: Why must filtered HCO3− be converted to CO2 to be reabsorbed?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why must filtered HCO3− be converted to CO2 to be reabsorbed?
options: HCO3− is too large to filter
HCO3− cannot cross the tubule membrane
body.explanation: HCO3− cannot cross; CO2 can, and HCO3− is rebuilt inside the cell.

title: Which are the ways to increase whole-muscle force? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are the ways to increase whole-muscle force? (choose all)
body.explanation: Force rises by recruiting more motor units and by increasing frequency (force-frequency).

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: LDL. VLDLs become LDLs containing mainly cholesterol; cells take them up by receptor-mediated endocytosis.

title: Why is a lost light reflex after head trauma serious?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why is a lost light reflex after head trauma serious?
options: It means the lens has failed
It means the cornea is scarred
body.explanation: The light reflex centres sit in the brainstem beside the vital centres, so its loss suggests brainstem injury.

title: During contraction, which region keeps the same length?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: During contraction, which region keeps the same length?
body.explanation: It equals the thick filament length.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Structural proteins. Titin is elastic and anchors myosin to the Z disc; nebulin is non-elastic along actin; CapZ caps actin at the Z disc.

title: Which factor increases taste and smell disorders?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which factor increases taste and smell disorders?
body.explanation: Prevalence of both disorders increases with age, reaching 13.9 percent in institutionalised older adults.

title: How does afferent arteriole dilation affect GFR?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How does afferent arteriole dilation affect GFR?
body.explanation: Textbook physiology: afferent dilation or efferent constriction raises glomerular pressure and GFR; afferent constriction lowers it.

title: What carries urine from the kidneys to the bladder?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What carries urine from the kidneys to the bladder?
body.explanation: The ureters transport urine from the kidneys to the bladder.

title: Two-point discrimination is best in areas with:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Two-point discrimination is best in areas with:
body.explanation: Fingertips.

title: Light-driven ATP production in plants is called:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Light-driven ATP production in plants is called:
body.explanation: Photophosphorylation in the light-dependent reactions.

title: What does hyperreflexia usually indicate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does hyperreflexia usually indicate?
body.explanation: Hyperactive or clonic reflexes indicate interruption of corticospinal and other descending pathways above the reflex level.

title: Strength training increases muscle size mainly by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Strength training increases muscle size mainly by:
options: Increasing the number of motor neurons
body.explanation: Fibre number is fixed at birth.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
options: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Descending limb of the loop of Henle. Aquaporins let water leave the filtrate into the interstitial fluid.

title: What are the functions of aqueous humour? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What are the functions of aqueous humour? (choose all)
body.explanation: It nourishes the lens and cornea and maintains intraocular pressure.

title: What forms the filtration slits?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What forms the filtration slits?
body.explanation: Podocyte extensions (pedicels) wrap the capillaries, leaving negatively charged 30 nm slits.

title: Indirect (second-messenger) receptors are characterised by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Indirect (second-messenger) receptors are characterised by:
options: Use only by amino acid transmitters
body.explanation: G protein, adenylate cyclase, cAMP.

title: What causes astigmatism?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What causes astigmatism?
body.explanation: Astigmatism comes from loss of smoothness of the cornea or lens surface and is corrected with cylindrical lenses.

title: HDL is too low in men below:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: HDL is too low in men below:
body.explanation: Too low: below 1.0 (men), 1.2 (women).

title: What releases Ca2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What releases Ca2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum?
body.explanation: The ryanodine receptor on the SR releases Ca2+ into the cytosol. SERCA pumps it back.

title: Leptin acts on melanocortin neurons by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Leptin acts on melanocortin neurons by:
body.explanation: Leptin stimulates melanocortin secretion.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the retina.

title: What determines which muscle contracts in a reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What determines which muscle contracts in a reflex?
body.explanation: The precise location of the stimulus fixes which muscle contracts; its strength sets the amplitude of the response. Reflexes are graded behaviours.

title: What is a myotome?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is a myotome?
body.explanation: Each set of spinal nerves innervates a set of muscles; testing them assesses nerve damage.

title: Leukocytes in the urine are called:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Leukocytes in the urine are called:
body.explanation: Pyuria = leukocytes; haematuria = erythrocytes.

title: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the muscle spindle (stretch receptor). The fully labelled arc is on the Visual tab.

title: Which afferents carry the phasic response?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which afferents carry the phasic response?
body.explanation: A dynamic change in length, such as a tendon tap, triggers a transient phasic contraction through Ia afferents.

title: Which lipoprotein is richest in cholesterol (about 53%)?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which lipoprotein is richest in cholesterol (about 53%)?
body.explanation: LDL contains mainly cholesterol.

title: Increasing alveolar ventilation will:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Increasing alveolar ventilation will:
body.explanation: More ventilation removes CO2 and raises pH.

title: Which force favours filtration?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which force favours filtration?
body.explanation: Blood hydrostatic pressure drives filtration; colloid osmotic pressure and capsular hydrostatic pressure oppose it.

title: What causes the falling phase of the action potential?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What causes the falling phase of the action potential?
body.explanation: Rising phase: Na+ rushes in. Falling phase: K+ leaves through the slow voltage-gated K+ channels, which close late and cause the dip below rest.

title: Which processes in the lecture directly use ATP?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which processes in the lecture directly use ATP?
body.explanation: Pumps and myosin use ATP; osmosis does not.

title: Saturated fatty acids have:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Saturated fatty acids have:
body.explanation: Saturated: all single C-C bonds.

title: Acetylcholine is inhibitory in cardiac muscle because it acts on:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Acetylcholine is inhibitory in cardiac muscle because it acts on:
body.explanation: The receptor decides the effect.

title: In pH = 6.1 + log [HCO3−]/(0.03 × PCO2), PCO2 is regulated by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In pH = 6.1 + log [HCO3−]/(0.03 × PCO2), PCO2 is regulated by:
body.explanation: PCO2: lungs; HCO3−: kidneys.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: CO2 and water. Carbon dioxide, controlled by the lungs (ventilation).

title: The main role of HDL is to:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The main role of HDL is to:
options: Remove excess cholesterol to the liver
Carry dietary triglyceride from the gut
body.explanation: HDL picks up cholesterol and returns it to the liver.

title: HDL cholesterol is converted by the liver into:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: HDL cholesterol is converted by the liver into:
body.explanation: The liver converts HDL cholesterol into bile salts.

title: Which are quantitative olfactory disorders? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are quantitative olfactory disorders? (choose all)
body.explanation: Quantitative: hyposmia and anosmia. Qualitative: parosmia, phantosmia, cacosmia.

title: What is the mechanism of referred pain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the mechanism of referred pain?
body.explanation: Visceral pain fibres synapse on the same second-order neurons as skin fibres, so the brain reads visceral pain as coming from the skin: the convergence-projection theory.

title: Which is a structural (not contractile) protein?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is a structural (not contractile) protein?
body.explanation: Troponin is regulatory.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Sodium release. Three Na+ are released outside (extracellular Na+ about 140 mM).

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Hydrogen ion and bicarbonate. H+ secretion and HCO3− reabsorption are controlled by the kidneys.

title: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the falling phase: k+ flows out. The fully labelled graph is on the Visual tab.

title: Which receptor does ACh act on at parasympathetic targets?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which receptor does ACh act on at parasympathetic targets?
body.explanation: Parasympathetic postganglionic fibres release ACh onto muscarinic receptors, which are G-protein coupled.

title: If arterial pressure falls, the afferent arteriole:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: If arterial pressure falls, the afferent arteriole:
body.explanation: It dilates so flow and filtration stay stable.

title: Fluid leaving the proximal tubule is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Fluid leaving the proximal tubule is:
body.explanation: Reduced to one third of its volume but still isosmotic.

title: Which adrenal zone makes aldosterone?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which adrenal zone makes aldosterone?
body.explanation: Glomerulosa: mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone. Fasciculata: glucocorticoids and androgens. Reticularis: androgens and glucocorticoids. Medulla: catecholamines.

title: Where does the neospinothalamic tract mainly end?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where does the neospinothalamic tract mainly end?
body.explanation: Most neospinothalamic fibres run to the ventrobasal complex of the thalamus, then to the somatosensory cortex.

title: Normal blood glucose is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Normal blood glucose is:

title: Where do C fibres terminate in the dorsal horn?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where do C fibres terminate in the dorsal horn?
body.explanation: C fibres end in laminae 1 and 2; A-delta in 1 and 5. Second-order axons from laminae 1 and 5 cross and ascend in the anterolateral column.

title: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is:
options: Permeable to water, impermeable to solutes
Permeable to solutes, impermeable to water
The site of active NaCl pumping
body.explanation: Descending: water leaves; ions stay.

title: Which muscle responds in the Achilles reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which muscle responds in the Achilles reflex?
body.explanation: Patellar: quadriceps, leg extension. Achilles: soleus, foot extension. Bicipital: biceps, forearm flexion. Tricipital: triceps, forearm extension.

title: Which are cardiovascular effects of chronic stress? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are cardiovascular effects of chronic stress? (choose all)
body.explanation: Coronary disease, ischaemia, infarction, heart failure, sudden death, tachycardia, dysrhythmias and hypertension.

title: Which can damage the filtration membrane? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which can damage the filtration membrane? (choose all)
body.explanation: Infection and trauma can let albumin or blood cells through.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Salt and water retention. Na+ and H2O reabsorption in the DCT and collecting duct raises plasma volume and blood pressure.

title: What happens when stereocilia bend toward the tallest row?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What happens when stereocilia bend toward the tallest row?
body.explanation: Deflection toward the tallest row increases channel opening (depolarisation); away from it decreases it.

title: The ascending limb is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The ascending limb is:
options: Permeable to water, not to solutes
Impermeable to water, pumps out Na+
The main site of aquaporin-2 insertion
The main site of glucose reabsorption
body.explanation: Ascending limb: active Na+ transport, Cl− follows, impermeable to water.

title: Which fibres carry second (burning) pain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which fibres carry second (burning) pain?
body.explanation: First, sharp pain travels in myelinated A-delta fibres; second, dull burning pain in unmyelinated C fibres.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Satiety. Wild type: leptin → satiety → food intake regulation.

title: The final 15% of water reabsorption is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The final 15% of water reabsorption is:
body.explanation: The final 15% is absorbed later in the nephron under hormonal control.

title: What is nociception?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is nociception?
body.explanation: The IASP defines nociception as the unconscious activity induced by a harmful stimulus; pain is the unpleasant sensory and emotional experience.

title: How are the three canals oriented?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How are the three canals oriented?
body.explanation: Being roughly perpendicular, together they detect every direction of rotation.

title: Melanocortins (α-MSH) act on which receptors to inhibit eating?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Melanocortins (α-MSH) act on which receptors to inhibit eating?
body.explanation: α-MSH acts on MC3/MC4 receptors in the paraventricular nucleus.

title: ADH increases water reabsorption by inserting which channel in the apical membrane?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: ADH increases water reabsorption by inserting which channel in the apical membrane?
body.explanation: ADH → cAMP → AQP2 inserted in the apical membrane of collecting duct cells.

title: Catabolic reactions are:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Catabolic reactions are:
body.explanation: Catabolism releases energy (exergonic) and heat (exothermic).

title: What makes a channel pore selective for anions?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What makes a channel pore selective for anions?
options: A negative charge inside the pore
A positive charge inside the pore
body.explanation: Charge selectivity: a positive charge in the pore repels cations, so the channel passes anions, and vice versa. Size selectivity then separates ions within a charge class.

title: What fluid bathes the apical surface of the hair cells?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What fluid bathes the apical surface of the hair cells?
body.explanation: Apices are bathed in endolymph, separated by tight junctions from the perilymph around the basolateral surfaces.

title: Jens Skou won the 1997 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Jens Skou won the 1997 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for:
options: The enzymatic mechanism of ATP synthase
The ionic basis of the action potential
body.explanation: Skou: Na+,K+-ATPase; Boyer and Walker: ATP synthase mechanism.

title: Which enzyme is deficient in McArdle disease?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which enzyme is deficient in McArdle disease?
body.explanation: Type V GSD: cramps, fatigue and myoglobinuria on exercise, no lactate rise, and a characteristic second wind. Tarui (type VII) lacks muscle PFK.

title: Which are cardiovascular fight-or-flight effects? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are cardiovascular fight-or-flight effects? (choose all)
body.explanation: Heart rate, contractility, cardiac output and pressure rise; blood shifts to muscle and heart, away from gut and kidneys.

title: Which statement about skeletal muscle fibres is correct?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which statement about skeletal muscle fibres is correct?
options: They are multinucleate with peripheral nuclei
They are joined by gap junctions
body.explanation: Formed by fusion of 100+ myoblasts.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Thin filament. Actin polymer with the regulatory proteins tropomyosin and troponin; about 8 nm wide.

title: Why is calcium partly not filtered?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why is calcium partly not filtered?
body.explanation: Some small substances such as calcium, iron and thyroid hormone are protein-bound and cannot cross.

title: Glucose is reabsorbed with Na+ by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Glucose is reabsorbed with Na+ by:
body.explanation: Sodium-glucose transport (SGLT) proteins; normally all glucose is reabsorbed.

title: About how much glycogen can the body store?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: About how much glycogen can the body store?
body.explanation: About 500 g, 75% in skeletal muscle and the rest in liver.

title: What is resilience?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is resilience?
body.explanation: Resilience: bouncing back from the initial negative effects. Hardiness: coping successfully and remaining healthy.

title: Which vitamin do the kidneys help activate to regulate calcium?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which vitamin do the kidneys help activate to regulate calcium?
body.explanation: The kidneys take part in calcitriol (vitamin D) synthesis.

title: Metabolism is defined as:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Metabolism is defined as:
options: The sum of all body chemical reactions
body.explanation: Metabolism denotes the sum of all body chemical reactions.

title: Which nucleus drives pupillary constriction in the light reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which nucleus drives pupillary constriction in the light reflex?
body.explanation: Optic nerve to the pretectal area, then the Edinger-Westphal nucleus of CN III, then via the ciliary ganglion to the constrictors. Dark dilation is sympathetic via the cervical ganglion.

title: What happens to the parasympathetic system in acute stress?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What happens to the parasympathetic system in acute stress?
body.explanation: In fight or flight the SN, SAM and HPA systems are activated and the parasympathetic system is diminished.

title: What is the most important way to control whole-muscle tension?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the most important way to control whole-muscle tension?
body.explanation: Recruitment of motor units is the main means; the other is raising stimulation frequency.

title: Acetylcholinesterase splits acetylcholine into:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Acetylcholinesterase splits acetylcholine into:
body.explanation: Choline is recycled; ChAT rebuilds ACh.

title: What voltage change does one vesicle produce?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What voltage change does one vesicle produce?
body.explanation: One vesicle gives a miniature end plate potential of about 0.5 mV. About 100 vesicles sum to an EPP of about 50 mV, enough to reach threshold.

title: How is a normal reflex graded?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How is a normal reflex graded?
body.explanation: 0 no response; 1+ diminished; 2+ normal; 3+ stronger than average; 4+ hyperactive.

title: Gluconeogenesis can use:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Gluconeogenesis can use:
body.explanation: Lactic acid, amino acids and the glycerol of triglycerides.
option_notes: Wrong: not listed as a glucose source.

title: Temporal summation occurs when:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Temporal summation occurs when:
options: Several presynaptic neurons fire at the same time
One presynaptic neuron fires repeatedly in quick succession
An EPSP and an IPSP cancel out
body.explanation: Same location, closer timing.

title: In sensitization, serotonin increases transmitter release by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In sensitization, serotonin increases transmitter release by:
options: Opening more K⁺ channels, shortening the action potential
Blocking K⁺ channels via cAMP, prolonging the action potential
Blocking presynaptic Ca²⁺ channels via cGMP
Increasing acetylcholinesterase in the synaptic cleft

title: Average body fat in women is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Average body fat in women is about:
body.explanation: Men about 15%, women about 25%.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: ATP. Temporarily stores energy from catabolic reactions and transfers it to anabolic reactions.

title: Which muscles have the smallest motor units?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which muscles have the smallest motor units?
body.explanation: The fewer fibres per neuron, the finer the movement. Motor units range from about 50 to 500 fibres.

title: At what ATP depletion does peripheral fatigue occur?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: At what ATP depletion does peripheral fatigue occur?
body.explanation: At about 30 percent depletion the ADP/ATP ratio is too high for cross-bridges. Rigor mortis is complete depletion.

title: CCK is secreted by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: CCK is secreted by:
body.explanation: CCK: enteroendocrine cells of the duodenum and jejunum.

title: Myosin is a hexamer made of:

subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the posterior (dorsal) horn: sensory.

title: SSRIs act by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: SSRIs act by:

title: Turning the head right excites which lateral canal?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Turning the head right excites which lateral canal?
body.explanation: Excitation occurs on the side the head turns to, with inhibition on the other side.

title: Which structure produces CSF?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure produces CSF?
body.explanation: CSF is made by the choroid plexus, a modified vascular structure in the ventricles.

title: What is the substantia gelatinosa?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the substantia gelatinosa?
body.explanation: Laminae II and III of the dorsal horn together form the substantia gelatinosa, where the paleospinothalamic C fibres terminate.

title: RDAs differ from the list of essential nutrients because RDAs:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: RDAs differ from the list of essential nutrients because RDAs:
options: Are identical for every human being
Define how much and vary with age, sex, pregnancy
body.explanation: Essential nutrients define which; RDAs define how much and vary.

title: The PCT reabsorbs about what fraction of the glomerular filtrate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The PCT reabsorbs about what fraction of the glomerular filtrate?

title: What is a dermatome?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is a dermatome?
body.explanation: A dermatome is an area of skin whose cutaneous fibres all track back to the same spinal level; its fibres may travel in different cutaneous nerves.

title: A triad is formed by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A triad is formed by:
options: One T-tubule and two terminal cisternae

title: Where are new olfactory bulb neurons generated?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where are new olfactory bulb neurons generated?
body.explanation: They arise in the subventricular zone of the lateral ventricles and migrate to the bulbs via the rostral migratory stream.

title: Which photoreceptors are scotopic?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which photoreceptors are scotopic?
body.explanation: Rods serve dim-light black-and-white vision; cones are high-threshold, photopic and give colour.

title: What is parosmia?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is parosmia?
body.explanation: Parosmia: a familiar smell is distorted. Phantosmia: smell without odour. Cacosmia: all odours unpleasant.

title: For each H+ secreted by the tubule, the kidney reabsorbs:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: For each H+ secreted by the tubule, the kidney reabsorbs:
body.explanation: H+ secretion goes with HCO3− reabsorption: urine acidification = blood alkalinisation.

title: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the peak (about +30 to +35 mv). The fully labelled graph is on the Visual tab.

title: 'Empty' calories:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: 'Empty' calories:
options: Provide few nutrients and suppress appetite
Contain no usable energy at all
Are found mainly in dietary fibre
body.explanation: Sugar and alcohol give energy but few nutrients, and suppress appetite.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Electron transport chain. Cytochromes in the inner mitochondrial membrane; the proton gradient drives ATP synthase.

title: What does hyporeflexia usually indicate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does hyporeflexia usually indicate?
options: A lesion of the reflex arc itself
A lesion above the spinal level
body.explanation: An absent or diminished response usually means disease of the two-neuron arc: the sensory or motor nerve or its segment.

title: What is reciprocal inhibition?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is reciprocal inhibition?
body.explanation: Reflex contraction of the agonist is accompanied by inhibition of the antagonist through an inhibitory interneuron: in a knee jerk, the quadriceps contracts and the hamstrings relax.

title: What share of primary care visits relate to stress and lifestyle?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What share of primary care visits relate to stress and lifestyle?
body.explanation: It has been estimated that up to 70 percent of primary care visits are for stress and lifestyle problems.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Urethra. Carries urine from the bladder to the outside of the body.

title: The most important extracellular buffer is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The most important extracellular buffer is:
body.explanation: The bicarbonate buffer system.

title: In what ratio does the adrenal medulla release adrenaline and noradrenaline?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In what ratio does the adrenal medulla release adrenaline and noradrenaline?
body.explanation: Preganglionic fibres synapse directly on the adrenal gland via nicotinic receptors, and it releases adrenaline and noradrenaline 4:1.

title: 'Countercurrent' means:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: 'Countercurrent' means:
options: Fluid flows in opposite directions in adjoining tubes
Current moves against the ion gradient
body.explanation: Fluid in one limb flows opposite to the adjoining limb.

title: Why do cross-bridges stay locked in rigor mortis?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why do cross-bridges stay locked in rigor mortis?
body.explanation: With no ATP, Ca2+ cannot be pumped and cross-bridges cannot dissociate. It begins about 3 hours after death and lasts up to 72 hours.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Krebs (citric acid) cycle. In the mitochondrial matrix; enzymes strip H+ and electrons onto NAD+ and FAD.

title: Which are signs seen on ophthalmoscopy? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are signs seen on ophthalmoscopy? (choose all)
body.explanation: Papilloedema (raised intracranial pressure), optic atrophy (pale, enlarged disc) and macular degeneration are fundus findings.

title: Which reactions occur in a cell depends on:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which reactions occur in a cell depends on:
body.explanation: The exact reactions depend on which enzymes are active at that time.

title: What is the equilibrium potential of K+?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the equilibrium potential of K+?
body.explanation: K+ tends to leave down its concentration gradient while the negative interior holds it in; the two balance at about -90 mV. For Na+ the equilibrium is about +60 mV.

title: Which statement about cholesterol is correct?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which statement about cholesterol is correct?
options: It is a major fuel at 9 kcal/g
It is not used for energy
It is carried only in chylomicrons
body.explanation: Cholesterol is structural and regulatory, not an energy source; it gives membranes rigidity.

title: What is the resting membrane potential of a typical neuron?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the resting membrane potential of a typical neuron?
body.explanation: About -70 mV, due to intracellular negative proteins, moderate intracellular K+ and high extracellular Na+.

title: Which are effects of angiotensin II?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are effects of angiotensin II?
body.explanation: Ang II: vasoconstriction, efferent constriction, aldosterone, ADH, thirst, PCT reabsorption.

title: The kidneys keep plasma osmolarity at about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The kidneys keep plasma osmolarity at about:
body.explanation: Plasma osmolarity is kept at about 300 mOsm.

title: Leptin signalling can fail because of:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Leptin signalling can fail because of:
options: Abnormal transporter across the blood-brain barrier
body.explanation: Three failure points: production, transport, receptor.

title: What are the three functions of the nervous system?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What are the three functions of the nervous system?
body.explanation: The nervous system performs sensory input, integration and motor output.

title: Without ADH, urine output can reach about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Without ADH, urine output can reach about:
body.explanation: No ADH: 105 mL/min reabsorbed, urine 15 mL/min ≈ 22 500 mL/day.

title: How many refraction points are in the eye?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many refraction points are in the eye?
body.explanation: Air to cornea, cornea to aqueous humour, aqueous humour to lens, lens to vitreous humour.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
options: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Proximal convoluted tubule. Reabsorbs ions, water and nutrients; removes toxins and adjusts filtrate pH.

title: For which olfactory loss is causal treatment available?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: For which olfactory loss is causal treatment available?
body.explanation: Only olfactory dysfunction due to nasal disease has causal treatment: surgery or corticosteroids.

title: Under normal oxygen tension, hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Under normal oxygen tension, hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) is:
body.explanation: HIF is degraded at normal O2; in hypoxia it persists and promotes EPO and erythropoiesis.

title: Which is part of Selye's alarm reaction triad?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is part of Selye's alarm reaction triad?
body.explanation: The triad: enlarged, discharging adrenal cortex; involution of the thymus, spleen and lymph nodes; bleeding ulcers in the stomach and duodenum.

title: What fraction of the plasma entering the afferent arteriole is filtered?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What fraction of the plasma entering the afferent arteriole is filtered?
body.explanation: 20% is filtered; 80% continues to the peritubular capillaries.

title: Which tastes are innately aversive?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which tastes are innately aversive?
body.explanation: Sour and bitter signal acids and potential toxins and are rejected even by newborns.

title: Which are features of endurance training? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are features of endurance training? (choose all)
body.explanation: Little hypertrophy but more and larger mitochondria, glycogen, myoglobin, oxidative enzymes and capillaries.

title: Peter Mitchell described:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Peter Mitchell described:
options: The chemiosmotic mechanism of ATP synthesis
body.explanation: Chemiosmotic theory, Nobel Chemistry 1978.

title: Which are the three main components of pain physiology? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are the three main components of pain physiology? (choose all)
body.explanation: Pain physiology has three components: transduction, transmission and modulation (slide 15).
option_notes: Correct: a noxious stimulus is converted into electrical activity at the nociceptor.
Correct: the signal is conducted from the periphery to the cord, brainstem and brain.
Not a component; pain receptors adapt very little.
Correct: descending pathways and interneurons alter pain signals.

title: Receptor potentials differ from action potentials because they:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Receptor potentials differ from action potentials because they:
options: Are all-or-none and always the same size
Have no refractory period and can summate

title: What range of light can the human eye see?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What range of light can the human eye see?
body.explanation: Visible light runs from purple to red; ultraviolet and infrared are invisible.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: HDL. Empty shells from the liver pick up cholesterol from tissues and return it to the liver.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Saltier interstitium. The medullary interstitium becomes more concentrated deeper in the medulla.

title: How many amino acids are essential?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many amino acids are essential?
body.explanation: Nine essential amino acids.

title: Aldosterone promotes Na+ and water reabsorption mainly in:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Aldosterone promotes Na+ and water reabsorption mainly in:
body.explanation: Aldosterone acts on the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct.

title: What does the vestibular apparatus detect?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does the vestibular apparatus detect?
body.explanation: It detects orientation and motion of the head, not the body, and relays them to the vestibular nuclei and cerebellum via CN VIII.

title: What gives the maculae their sensitivity to gravity?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What gives the maculae their sensitivity to gravity?
body.explanation: The otoconial crystals pull on the membrane and bend the stereocilia, signalling static head orientation.

title: Where is fast-sharp pain NOT felt?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where is fast-sharp pain NOT felt?
body.explanation: Fast pain arises from needle pricks, cuts, burns and electric shock in the skin; it is not felt in deeper tissues.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Sarcomere. The functional unit, from one Z disc to the next; it shortens during contraction.

title: The body's main source of metabolic water is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The body's main source of metabolic water is:
options: Oxygen reduction at the end of the ETC
body.explanation: Each O atom accepts 2 e− and 2 H+ forming water.

title: How is GFR calculated?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How is GFR calculated?
body.explanation: GFR = net filtration pressure x filtration coefficient; Kf depends on the permeability and surface area of the barrier.

title: Which is the smallest lipoprotein?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is the smallest lipoprotein?
body.explanation: HDL 5-12 nm; chylomicrons up to 1 200 nm.

title: One calorie is the heat needed to raise:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: One calorie is the heat needed to raise:
body.explanation: 1 calorie: 1 g of water by 1 °C.

title: DNP (dinitrophenol) acts as:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: DNP (dinitrophenol) acts as:
options: A protonophore that uncouples ATP synthesis
An inhibitor of hexokinase in glycolysis
body.explanation: DNP lets H+ return to the matrix without passing ATP synthase.

title: Which zone of the neuron initiates action potentials?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which zone of the neuron initiates action potentials?
body.explanation: Four zones: input (dendrites and cell body), trigger (axon hillock), conducting (axon) and output (axon terminals).

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the ach vesicles (about 1000 ach each). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Intracellular K+ concentration is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Intracellular K+ concentration is about:
body.explanation: Inside K+ about 140 mM; outside 5 mM.

title: Which are parasympathetic effects? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are parasympathetic effects? (choose all)
body.explanation: Parasympathetic: constricted pupils, copious saliva, more gut motility, slower heart, constricted bronchi.

title: How is the spindle arranged relative to the muscle?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How is the spindle arranged relative to the muscle?
body.explanation: Spindles lie in parallel with the skeletal muscle, so contraction unloads them and stretch stimulates them.

title: In an isometric contraction:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In an isometric contraction:

title: NAD+ is derived from:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: NAD+ is derived from:
body.explanation: NAD+ from niacin (B vitamin); FAD from riboflavin.

title: What causes presbyopia?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What causes presbyopia?
body.explanation: Lens proteins denature with age, so the lens loses elasticity and accommodation, impairing near vision; accommodation nears zero after 70.

title: Which enzyme releases free glucose into the blood (liver, kidney, intestine)?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which enzyme releases free glucose into the blood (liver, kidney, intestine)?
body.explanation: Glucose 6-phosphatase is found in liver, kidney and intestinal cells.

title: Which tracts are motor indirect pathways? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which tracts are motor indirect pathways? (choose all)
body.explanation: Indirect: rubrospinal, tectospinal, vestibulospinal, lateral and medial reticulospinal. Direct: lateral and anterior corticospinal and corticobulbar.

title: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the rising phase: na+ rushes in. The fully labelled graph is on the Visual tab.

title: What triggers ACh release from the nerve terminal?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What triggers ACh release from the nerve terminal?
options: Binding of ACh to the terminal
body.explanation: The action potential opens voltage-gated Ca2+ channels; Ca2+ entry releases ACh, which diffuses and binds the receptor.

title: What happens to the lens when the ciliary muscles contract?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What happens to the lens when the ciliary muscles contract?
body.explanation: Ciliary contraction relaxes the zonular fibres, so the lens rounds up, increasing refractive power for near vision.

title: In juxtamedullary nephrons the efferent arteriole branches into:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In juxtamedullary nephrons the efferent arteriole branches into:
options: Vasa recta around the long loop
body.explanation: Juxtamedullary: vasa recta; cortical: peritubular capillaries.

title: Effects of cyanide:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Effects of cyanide:
options: Heat production is the main effect
body.explanation: Cyanide inhibits respiration; heat is not its defining effect.

title: What is cortisol's effect on insulin?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is cortisol's effect on insulin?
body.explanation: Cortisol is anti-insulin, permissive for glucagon and catecholamines, raises vascular alpha receptors, is anti-inflammatory and regulates renal water excretion.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the posterior (dorsal) horn: sensory.

title: Which muscles does the anterior canal drive in the VOR?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which muscles does the anterior canal drive in the VOR?
body.explanation: The anterior canal influences the ipsilateral superior rectus and the contralateral inferior oblique.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Calcium entry. Depolarization of the terminal opens voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels; Ca²⁺ entry is the trigger for release.

title: Which enzyme removes lipids from chylomicrons?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which enzyme removes lipids from chylomicrons?
body.explanation: Lipoprotein lipase.

title: Acidosis causes which potassium disorder?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Acidosis causes which potassium disorder?
body.explanation: Acidosis shifts K+ from the intracellular to the extracellular space: hyperkalaemia.

title: Which muscle type has the fastest myosin ATPase?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which muscle type has the fastest myosin ATPase?
body.explanation: Smooth is slowest, cardiac intermediate.

title: Which blood variables do the kidneys regulate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which blood variables do the kidneys regulate?
body.explanation: Volume, pressure, osmolarity, electrolytes and acid-base (H+/HCO3−).

title: What do photosynthesis and respiration have in common?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do photosynthesis and respiration have in common?
options: Both release oxygen as a product
Electron transport, a proton gradient, ATP synthase
Both take place in the cytoplasm only
Both use NADP+ as electron acceptor
body.explanation: Both rely on electron transport, a proton gradient and ATP synthase.

title: Which segments are the centre of the patellar reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which segments are the centre of the patellar reflex?
body.explanation: The patellar reflex depends on L2 to L4. It is often absent in chronic diabetes or neurosyphilis and exaggerated with descending motor tract disease.

title: How many nephrons does each kidney contain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many nephrons does each kidney contain?
body.explanation: Each kidney has over 1 million nephrons.

title: What do sympathetic fibres to the renal vessels release?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do sympathetic fibres to the renal vessels release?
body.explanation: Postganglionic neurons to the renal vascular smooth muscle release dopamine, the second exception.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
options: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
Descending limb of the loop of Henle
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Collecting duct. Reabsorbs solutes and water from the filtrate; water permeability set by ADH.

title: Filtrate enters the capsular space through:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Filtrate enters the capsular space through:
body.explanation: Clefts between foot processes are filtration slits, where filtrate enters the capsular space.

title: What makes up the CNS?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What makes up the CNS?
body.explanation: The brain and spinal cord form the CNS; nerves, ganglia and sensory organs form the PNS.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Aldosterone. Angiotensin II stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete aldosterone.

title: PYY is secreted by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: PYY is secreted by:
body.explanation: PYY: enteroendocrine cells of the ileum and colon.

title: Which receptor senses hot water and capsaicin?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which receptor senses hot water and capsaicin?
body.explanation: Your professor's own question: TRPV1 senses hot water and capsaicin.

title: What is the role of the tonic phase?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the role of the tonic phase?
body.explanation: The tonic phase keeps the anti-gravity muscles of neck, trunk and legs active. The weight of the head stretches the neck extensors, which contract reflexly: muscle tone.

title: The defining effect of DNP is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The defining effect of DNP is:
body.explanation: Energy is released as heat instead of ATP.

title: Which are roles of the myotatic reflex? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are roles of the myotatic reflex? (choose all)
body.explanation: Maintaining tone, adjusting posture, adapting muscle function during exercise and preventing injury from overstretching.

title: Apical Na+ symports in the PCT are:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Apical Na+ symports in the PCT are:
body.explanation: They use the Na+ gradient made by the basal pumps: secondary active transport.

title: In the US, about what share of people is obese?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In the US, about what share of people is obese?
body.explanation: 30% obese, another 35% overweight.

title: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the threshold (-50 to -55 mv). The fully labelled graph is on the Visual tab.

title: What do the semicircular canals detect?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do the semicircular canals detect?
body.explanation: They detect angular accelerations from rotation of the head or body.

title: Where is ADH released from?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where is ADH released from?
body.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) is released from the posterior pituitary.

title: Where are the vestibular nerve cell bodies?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where are the vestibular nerve cell bodies?
body.explanation: Bipolar neurons in the vestibular ganglion, in the lateral internal acoustic meatus.

title: What does enkephalin do in the dorsal horn? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does enkephalin do in the dorsal horn? (choose all)
body.explanation: Your professor's question: it inhibits Ca2+ influx and transmitter release, raises K+ efflux and hyperpolarises the second-order neuron: all of the above.

title: Which does the superior vestibular division supply? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which does the superior vestibular division supply? (choose all)
body.explanation: Superior: lateral and anterior cristae, most of the utricle and part of the saccule.

title: Which are routes of body water loss?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are routes of body water loss?
body.explanation: Urine, sweat, breath, faeces (diarrhoea), bleeding, vomiting, rhinorrhoea, tears.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Ending the signal. Active reuptake into the terminal or glia, enzymatic breakdown (acetylcholinesterase) and diffusion out of the cleft.

title: What is the visual acuity of an emmetropic eye?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the visual acuity of an emmetropic eye?
body.explanation: Letter charts are read at 20 feet (6 m). Seeing only the largest letter gives 20/200, one tenth of normal.

title: Which molecule couples catabolic and anabolic reactions?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which molecule couples catabolic and anabolic reactions?
body.explanation: ATP transfers energy from catabolic to anabolic reactions.

title: Thick filaments are made of:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Thick filaments are made of:
body.explanation: About 250 myosin II molecules.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Axon hillock. Keeps score of all EPSPs and IPSPs; an action potential fires only if the sum reaches threshold (-50 to -55 mV).

title: Which is a short-term hunger signal?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is a short-term hunger signal?
body.explanation: Ghrelin is the short-term hunger (orexigenic) hormone.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the thalamus.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: VLDL. Very low-density lipoproteins produced by the liver.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Bladder. Stores urine until it is voided.

title: Which molecules pass freely through the filtration membrane?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which molecules pass freely through the filtration membrane?
body.explanation: Water, electrolytes, glucose, fatty acids, amino acids, nitrogenous wastes and vitamins, all under about 3 nm.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal.

title: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the integrating centre. The fully labelled arc is on the Visual tab.

title: Creatinine is the breakdown product of:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Creatinine is the breakdown product of:
body.explanation: Creatinine comes from creatine phosphate catabolism.

title: Which drug blocks the salty taste channel?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which drug blocks the salty taste channel?
body.explanation: Salt enters through a selective Na+ channel, passing only Na+ and Li+, blocked by the diuretic amiloride.

title: Which segment reabsorbs Na+ and Cl− into the interstitium?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which segment reabsorbs Na+ and Cl− into the interstitium?
options: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
