Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
body.explanation: The ascending limb reabsorbs Na+ and Cl−.

title: What is the consensual light reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the consensual light reflex?
body.explanation: Light in one eye constricts that pupil (direct) and the other (consensual or indirect), because the optic pathways decussate.

title: What is phantogeusia?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is phantogeusia?
body.explanation: Phantogeusia: a persistent, usually unpleasant taste without any stimulus. Parageusia: distorted taste.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Glycolysis. Ten steps in the cytoplasm; glucose → 2 pyruvic acid, net 2 ATP, 2 NADH.

title: At what temperature is TRPV1 activated?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: At what temperature is TRPV1 activated?
body.explanation: TRPV1 (VR-1), on C and A-delta fibres, responds to about 45°C and to capsaicin. TRPV2 needs about 52°C, ignores capsaicin, and is on A-delta fibres.

title: Alcohol provides about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Alcohol provides about:
body.explanation: Alcohol 7 kcal/g; sugar and alcohol are empty calories.

title: Why does an exercising ischaemic muscle hurt so fast?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why does an exercising ischaemic muscle hurt so fast?
body.explanation: Pain appears within 15 to 20 s if the ischaemic muscle is exercised, versus 3 to 4 minutes at rest; lactic acid, bradykinin and proteolytic enzymes stimulate the endings.

title: In photosynthesis, which molecule is oxidised to release oxygen?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In photosynthesis, which molecule is oxidised to release oxygen?
body.explanation: H2O is oxidised, O2 is produced and NADPH generated.

title: Water as a nutrient:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Water as a nutrient:
options: Is synthesised in sufficient amounts by the body
Must be consumed in the diet
body.explanation: Water must be consumed in the diet; it is a macronutrient.

title: How wide are the pores of the glomerular endothelium?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How wide are the pores of the glomerular endothelium?
body.explanation: The fenestrated endothelium has 70 to 90 nm pores: small enough to exclude blood cells, highly permeable.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Formation of acetyl-CoA. Oxidation of pyruvate gives 2 acetyl-CoA per glucose.

title: Which inputs does the CNS integrate for balance? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which inputs does the CNS integrate for balance? (choose all)
body.explanation: Visual, vestibular and proprioceptive input, integrated especially by the cerebellum.

title: Which influence taste perception? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which influence taste perception? (choose all)
body.explanation: Odour, temperature, texture and past experience with food all shape taste.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Angiotensin II. Angiotensin-converting enzyme in the lungs and kidneys converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the optic nerve.

title: The myogenic mechanism is also called:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The myogenic mechanism is also called:
body.explanation: Myogenic mechanism = Bayliss effect.

title: Which cells contain renin granules and sense blood pressure?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which cells contain renin granules and sense blood pressure?
body.explanation: Granular cells are mechanoreceptors in the afferent arteriole with renin granules.

title: How is ion flux through a channel described?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How is ion flux through a channel described?
body.explanation: Ion flux through a channel is always passive, down the electrochemical gradient, up to a million ions per second.

title: Glucose in the urine is called:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Glucose in the urine is called:
body.explanation: Glucose in urine: glucosuria.

title: Most stored glycogen is in:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Most stored glycogen is in:
body.explanation: 75% in skeletal muscle fibres.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the pituitary gland (via infundibulum).

title: How often does the total plasma volume pass the filter each day?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How often does the total plasma volume pass the filter each day?
body.explanation: The filtrate formed daily equals 50 to 60 times the body's blood volume.

title: Where is CRH produced?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where is CRH produced?
body.explanation: CRH comes from the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus and is the major stimulus for ACTH.

title: Who first described stress, and when?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Who first described stress, and when?
body.explanation: Selye described stress in 1936 as the nonspecific response of the body to any demand: the general adaptation syndrome.

title: Which part of the loop sets up the concentration gradient?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of the loop sets up the concentration gradient?
body.explanation: The ascending portion sets up the gradient.

title: At what speed do A-delta fibres conduct?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: At what speed do A-delta fibres conduct?
body.explanation: A-delta fibres carry fast pain at 6 to 30 m/s; unmyelinated C fibres carry slow pain at 0.5 to 2 m/s.

title: By how much does olfactory neurogenesis fall with age in mice?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: By how much does olfactory neurogenesis fall with age in mice?
body.explanation: Neurogenesis in the olfactory epithelium declines by about 90 percent between 3 and 16 months in mice.

title: Eating less than how much fat per day risks vitamin deficiency?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Eating less than how much fat per day risks vitamin deficiency?
body.explanation: Less than 20 g of fat per day.

title: Benefits of cellulose (fibre) include:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Benefits of cellulose (fibre) include:
options: Filling the stomach and reducing intake
body.explanation: Fibre slows digestion, prevents constipation, fills the stomach, lowers heart risk.

title: Leptin is secreted by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Leptin is secreted by:
body.explanation: Leptin is made by adipose cells.

title: Which gland part releases epinephrine?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which gland part releases epinephrine?
body.explanation: The adrenal medulla releases epinephrine, norepinephrine and dopamine.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Fascicle. A bundle of muscle fibres wrapped in perimysium.

title: The source of Ca²⁺ for skeletal muscle contraction is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The source of Ca²⁺ for skeletal muscle contraction is:
body.explanation: Smooth and cardiac also use ECF.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the synaptic cleft (about 50 nm). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: pH is defined as:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: pH is defined as:
body.explanation: pH = −log [H+].

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Kidneys. Retroperitoneal organs that filter plasma and form urine.

title: In the proximal tubule, SGLT relies on:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In the proximal tubule, SGLT relies on:
options: Direct ATP hydrolysis by SGLT itself
The Na+ gradient made by the basal Na+/K+ pump
The proton gradient of the H+-ATPase
body.explanation: SGLT is secondary active transport powered by the Na+ gradient.

title: Leptin is a:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Leptin is a:
options: Short-term satiety regulator from the ileum
body.explanation: Leptin is a long-term regulator; ghrelin short-term.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
options: Lateral horn (T1 to L2, S2 to S4)
body.explanation: The arrow points to the grey matter (butterfly).

title: How many ACh molecules does one vesicle contain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many ACh molecules does one vesicle contain?
body.explanation: Each vesicle holds a fixed amount of ACh, about 1000 molecules.

title: Olfactory loss is an early sign of which diseases?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Olfactory loss is an early sign of which diseases?
body.explanation: Olfactory dysfunction is an early symptom of idiopathic Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's dementia.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Muscle fibre. One multinucleate cell formed by fusion of 100 or more myoblasts; its number is fixed at birth.

title: What fraction of the filtrate is reabsorbed?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What fraction of the filtrate is reabsorbed?
body.explanation: Only about 1 to 2 L (1.5 L) of urine is excreted daily, so 99 percent is reabsorbed.

title: Which are proprioceptors? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are proprioceptors? (choose all)
body.explanation: Proprioceptors include the spindle, the Golgi tendon organ, joint kinesthetic receptors and the vestibular apparatus.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Leptin receptor. Abnormal Ob-R: high leptin yet obesity (leptin resistance).

title: How is ACh removed from the cleft?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How is ACh removed from the cleft?
body.explanation: AChE on the end plate breaks ACh into acetate and choline; choline is taken back up. AChE is not regulated, so longer stimulation needs more ACh.

title: Which fibres mediate fast pain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which fibres mediate fast pain?
body.explanation: Your professor's own question: fast pain travels in A-delta fibres.

title: Mesangial cells:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Mesangial cells:
options: Regulate glomerular blood flow by contracting
body.explanation: Mesangial cells contract to regulate flow and engulf trapped macromolecules.

title: What causes glaucoma?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What causes glaucoma?
body.explanation: Obstruction raises aqueous volume and intraocular pressure, which can damage the lens and retina and cause loss of vision.

title: Why does a constricted pupil sharpen vision?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why does a constricted pupil sharpen vision?
body.explanation: Through a small pupil light rays come to focus quickly, raising acuity: depth of focus. The best acuity comes from rays within 5 degrees.

title: What do dendrites generate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do dendrites generate?
body.explanation: Dendrites conduct toward the cell body and generate local, graded potentials rather than action potentials.

title: An IPSP is typically produced by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: An IPSP is typically produced by:
body.explanation: Negative ions in hyperpolarize.

title: The four steps of cellular respiration in order are:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The four steps of cellular respiration in order are:
body.explanation: Glycolysis → acetyl-CoA → Krebs → electron transport chain.

title: Where does ACE mainly convert angiotensin I to angiotensin II?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where does ACE mainly convert angiotensin I to angiotensin II?
body.explanation: ACE (endothelium) in the lungs and kidneys.

title: NAD+ binds:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: NAD+ binds:
body.explanation: NAD+ + 2 H → NADH + H+: two electrons, one proton.

title: How soon is fast pain felt?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How soon is fast pain felt?
body.explanation: Fast pain is felt within about 0.1 s; slow pain begins after 1 s or more and builds over seconds to minutes.

title: What does the vestibulo-ocular reflex do?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does the vestibulo-ocular reflex do?
body.explanation: It rotates the eyes opposite to head movement so the retina stays steady; the flocculus drives its long-term adaptation.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Active NaCl pumping. The ascending limb actively transports Na+ (Cl− follows) and is impermeable to water.

title: What substance gives umami taste?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What substance gives umami taste?
body.explanation: Umami (savoury) is the taste of MSG. Quinine is the classic bitter tastant, HCl and tartaric acid sour, NaCl salty.

title: The Na+/K+-ATPase moves per ATP:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The Na+/K+-ATPase moves per ATP:
body.explanation: 3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in (3:2).

title: Where are physical stressors mainly processed?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where are physical stressors mainly processed?
body.explanation: Physical stressors are processed by brainstem and hypothalamic regions and need an immediate, almost reflexive response.

title: Compared with leptin, insulin's effect on appetite is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Compared with leptin, insulin's effect on appetite is:
body.explanation: Insulin is a weaker satiety signal than leptin.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Triad. One T-tubule between two terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, which store and release Ca²⁺.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the t-tubule (dhp receptor). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Potassium transport. Two K+ bind outside and are released inside (intracellular K+ about 140 mM, outside 5 mM).

title: Urea is formed mainly in:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Urea is formed mainly in:
body.explanation: Amino acids lose NH2 to form ammonia; the liver converts ammonia to urea.

title: Which stimuli cause visceral pain? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which stimuli cause visceral pain? (choose all)
body.explanation: Ischaemia, chemical damage, smooth muscle spasm, excess distension and stretching of connective tissue. Cutting the viscera does not.

title: Where are taste buds NOT found?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where are taste buds NOT found?
body.explanation: Taste buds lie on the dorsal and lateral tongue, soft palate, larynx, uvula, pharynx, epiglottis and upper oesophagus.

title: Urinary ammonia comes from:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Urinary ammonia comes from:
body.explanation: Ammonia comes from the deamination of amino acids.

title: Which lipoprotein is about 50% protein?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which lipoprotein is about 50% protein?
body.explanation: HDL: protein 50%.

title: Which hormones fall during prolonged stress?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which hormones fall during prolonged stress?
body.explanation: GH and prolactin, which enhance immunity, generally fall in prolonged stress; endorphins rise and are immunosuppressive.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
options: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Glomerulus. Filters small solutes from the blood into Bowman's capsule.

title: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the ia afferent (from the spindle). The fully labelled arc is on the Visual tab.

title: Which afferents come from the Golgi tendon organ?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which afferents come from the Golgi tendon organ?
body.explanation: Golgi tendon organs are low-threshold mechanoreceptors in tendons signalling changes in tension via group Ib afferents.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the ampulla.

title: Which is a physical stressor?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is a physical stressor?
body.explanation: Physical stressors actually disturb physiology, such as haemorrhage and infection. Psychological stressors threaten and are anticipated.

title: Which receptor on the T-tubule senses depolarization?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which receptor on the T-tubule senses depolarization?
body.explanation: L-type voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, the DHP receptors, open along the T-tubules and trigger the ryanodine receptors of the SR.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the anterior (ventral) horn: motor.

title: What is olfactory agnosia?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is olfactory agnosia?
body.explanation: Agnosia: odours are detected but cannot be classified or contrasted.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Receptor activation. Transmitter diffuses across the cleft and binds receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the motor nerve terminal. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Where is aqueous humour reabsorbed?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where is aqueous humour reabsorbed?
body.explanation: It is made by the ciliary body, fills the anterior chamber and drains through the canal of Schlemm, at the iris-cornea junction.

title: Substances passing between PCT cells use the:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Substances passing between PCT cells use the:
body.explanation: Paracellular = between cells, through leaky junctions.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the lens.

title: Obesity is defined in the lecture as weight more than:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Obesity is defined in the lecture as weight more than:
body.explanation: Obesity: weight more than 20% above the recommended norm for age, sex and height.

title: According to the lecture, which segment has aquaporins that let water pass from the filtrate into the interstitial fluid?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: According to the lecture, which segment has aquaporins that let water pass from the filtrate into the interstitial fluid?
options: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
Descending limb of the loop of Henle
body.explanation: Descending limb of the loop of Henle: aquaporins let water pass from the filtrate into the interstitial fluid.
option_notes: Reabsorbs Na+ and Cl−; impermeable to water.
Aquaporins let water leave the filtrate into the interstitium.
Filters plasma into the capsule; it does not reabsorb water from the filtrate.
Collects urine; no reabsorption of filtrate water.

title: Which intrafusal fibre types exist?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which intrafusal fibre types exist?
body.explanation: Three types: nuclear chain fibres, static nuclear bag fibres and dynamic nuclear bag fibres.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Myofibril. Lengthwise subdivision of the fibre, made of myofilaments in repeating sarcomeres.

title: Which statements about tubular reabsorption are correct?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which statements about tubular reabsorption are correct?
options: Reabsorbed fluid is taken up by peritubular capillaries
PCT cells have prominent microvilli and many mitochondria
PCT junctions are tight and block water
Cl− follows Na+ passively in the PCT
body.explanation: PCT junctions are leaky, letting water through.

title: What kind of cell is an olfactory receptor?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What kind of cell is an olfactory receptor?
body.explanation: Olfactory receptor cells are neurons, unlike taste cells, which are modified epithelial cells.

title: Children with congenital leptin deficiency are treated with:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Children with congenital leptin deficiency are treated with:
body.explanation: Recombinant leptin reverses the obesity.

title: What are pain receptors?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What are pain receptors?
body.explanation: All pain receptors in skin and tissues are free nerve endings, found in the skin, periosteum, arterial walls, joint surfaces and the falx and tentorium.

title: Which set the resting membrane potential? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which set the resting membrane potential? (choose all)
body.explanation: Negative proteins inside, moderate K+ inside and high Na+ outside give about -70 mV. Voltage-gated Na+ channels are closed at rest.

title: Which raise LDL according to the lecture?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which raise LDL according to the lecture?
body.explanation: Saturated fat, smoking, coffee and stress raise LDL; exercise improves HDL/LDL.

title: Fritz Lipmann shared the 1953 Nobel Prize for discovering:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Fritz Lipmann shared the 1953 Nobel Prize for discovering:
body.explanation: Lipmann: coenzyme A; Krebs: citric acid cycle (both 1953).

title: At what potential do voltage-gated Na+ channels open?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: At what potential do voltage-gated Na+ channels open?
body.explanation: Both voltage-gated Na+ and K+ channels are closed at -70 mV and open at about -50 to -55 mV; Na+ opens rapidly, K+ slowly.

title: How do smells change with continued exposure?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How do smells change with continued exposure?
body.explanation: Smells habituate rapidly.

title: Which circuit is critical for ending the stress response?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which circuit is critical for ending the stress response?
body.explanation: Cortisol acts on the hippocampus, which turns off the HPA response via the PVN; lesions prolong stress and raise PVN CRH.

title: What sets the size of a graded potential?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What sets the size of a graded potential?
options: It is always the same size
body.explanation: The deflection is proportional to the stimulus (V = IR). Graded potentials are local, vary in size and fade with distance.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Body functions. Normal function, homeostasis, repair and growth.

title: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of the reflex arc is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the dorsal root ganglion (sensory cell body). The fully labelled arc is on the Visual tab.

title: What sets the tension of a single fibre?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What sets the tension of a single fibre?
body.explanation: Single-fibre tension depends on the number of pivoting cross-bridges, the resting length at stimulation and the stimulation frequency.

title: Where do ions cross the membrane in a myelinated axon?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where do ions cross the membrane in a myelinated axon?
body.explanation: Voltage-gated channels cluster at the nodes of Ranvier, and the signal jumps node to node: saltatory conduction. It is faster and needs fewer Na+/K+ pumps.

title: Which afferent carries both static and dynamic information?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which afferent carries both static and dynamic information?
body.explanation: Ia (17 µm, 70 to 110 m/s) innervates both bag and chain fibres, signalling length and speed. II (8 µm, 30 to 70 m/s) mainly chain fibres, signalling length only.

title: The main stimulus for ANP secretion is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The main stimulus for ANP secretion is:
body.explanation: ANP is released when the atria are distended.

title: Which are nitrogenous wastes excreted by the kidney?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are nitrogenous wastes excreted by the kidney?
body.explanation: Urea, uric acid and creatinine are the nitrogenous wastes; glucose is normally fully reabsorbed.
option_notes: Wrong: not a waste; normally absent from urine.

title: What share of nephrons are cortical?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What share of nephrons are cortical?
body.explanation: Cortical nephrons 85%; juxtamedullary 15%.

title: How many receptor cells does a taste bud contain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many receptor cells does a taste bud contain?
body.explanation: Each taste bud contains about 100 taste receptor cells.

title: Which meningeal layer has spider-like trabeculae?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which meningeal layer has spider-like trabeculae?
body.explanation: Dura outermost, arachnoid in the middle with its trabeculae, pia closely applied to the brain. Where they separate, cisterns of CSF form.

title: What is a motor unit?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is a motor unit?
options: One motor neuron and its fibres
body.explanation: A motor unit is a single motor neuron and all the muscle fibres it innervates, which contract together. Each fibre is innervated by only one motor neuron.

title: How many intrafusal fibres does a spindle contain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How many intrafusal fibres does a spindle contain?
body.explanation: Muscle spindles consist of four to eight specialised intrafusal fibres.

title: Which part of myosin holds the ATP-binding site?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which part of myosin holds the ATP-binding site?

title: The cardiac Na+/Ca2+ exchanger ratio is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The cardiac Na+/Ca2+ exchanger ratio is:
body.explanation: Na+/Ca2+ exchanger 3:1.

title: ob/ob mice are obese because they:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: ob/ob mice are obese because they:
body.explanation: Defective ob gene → no leptin → no satiety.

title: What is the normal GFR in a man?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the normal GFR in a man?
body.explanation: About 125 mL/min or 180 L/day in men; about 105 mL/min or 150 L/day in women.

title: Which nucleus relays the analgesia system to the cord?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which nucleus relays the analgesia system to the cord?
body.explanation: Periaqueductal and periventricular grey, then the raphe magnus in the lower pons, then a pain-inhibitory complex in the dorsal horn.

title: Which type of reflex protects the body from injury?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which type of reflex protects the body from injury?
body.explanation: Somatic reflexes start at somatic sensory endings, act on skeletal muscle and protect from injury. Autonomic reflexes start in the viscera and act on soft tissue organs.

title: Fat provides about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Fat provides about:
body.explanation: Fat 9 kcal/g; carbohydrate 4 kcal/g.

title: How do pain receptors adapt?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How do pain receptors adapt?
body.explanation: They adapt very little; sometimes excitation grows as the stimulus continues, which keeps the person aware of ongoing damage.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Ureters. Transport urine from the kidneys to the bladder.

title: Normal GFR per minute is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Normal GFR per minute is about:
body.explanation: 2 mL/s, 120 mL/min.

title: Filtered bicarbonate load is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Filtered bicarbonate load is about:
body.explanation: About 4 320 mEq/day, nearly all reabsorbed.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Chylomicrons. Formed in the small intestine, absorbed by lymph, then drain into the blood; 90% triglyceride.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Lipoprotein lipase. Removes lipids from chylomicrons; triglycerides are stored in adipocytes or used by cells.

title: Which hormone made by the kidney stimulates red blood cell production?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which hormone made by the kidney stimulates red blood cell production?
body.explanation: Erythropoietin (EPO) stimulates erythropoiesis in the bone marrow.

title: Which organ stores urine until it is voided?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which organ stores urine until it is voided?
body.explanation: Ureters transport, the bladder stores, the urethra carries urine out.

title: About how much more water is reabsorbed in the descending limb?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: About how much more water is reabsorbed in the descending limb?
body.explanation: An additional 20%, continuously and without regulation.

title: Which are neuroglial cells? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are neuroglial cells? (choose all)
body.explanation: Neuroglia: ependymal cells, astrocytes, Schwann cells, oligodendrocytes and microglia.

title: What is alpha-gamma coactivation?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is alpha-gamma coactivation?
body.explanation: When alpha neurons contract the muscle, gamma neurons contract the spindle ends, so the spindle does not go slack.

title: The outer shell of a lipoprotein is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The outer shell of a lipoprotein is:
body.explanation: Polar proteins and amphipathic phospholipids make the shell hydrophilic.

title: Angiotensinogen is produced by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Angiotensinogen is produced by:
body.explanation: Angiotensinogen is a blood protein made by the liver.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Fall in blood pressure. Baroreceptors in the carotid and aorta stimulate the sympathetic nervous system.

title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2019 rewarded work on:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2019 rewarded work on:
options: How cells sense and adapt to oxygen
body.explanation: 2019: discoveries of how cells sense and adapt to oxygen availability (HIF).

title: Ghrelin is secreted by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Ghrelin is secreted by:
options: Parietal cells of the gastric fundus
body.explanation: Ghrelin: parietal cells of the gastric fundus.

title: A well-nourished adult meets what share of resting energy needs from fat?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A well-nourished adult meets what share of resting energy needs from fat?
body.explanation: 80 to 90% of resting energy comes from fat.

title: What are the two major cell categories of the nervous system?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What are the two major cell categories of the nervous system?
body.explanation: Neurons are the signalling cells; neuroglia support their development, growth, survival and structure.

title: The motor protein that bends cilia and flagella is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The motor protein that bends cilia and flagella is:
body.explanation: Kinesins move organelles.

title: When does a light ray not refract?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: When does a light ray not refract?
body.explanation: A ray hitting a surface perpendicularly is not refracted, whatever the indices; any deviation increases refraction.

title: What is Ménière's disease linked to?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is Ménière's disease linked to?
body.explanation: Spontaneous high afferent activity causes dizziness and nausea, the nausea via the vagal reflex pathway.

title: How does smooth muscle activate contraction?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How does smooth muscle activate contraction?
body.explanation: Smooth muscle uses Ca2+-calmodulin to activate MLCK, phosphorylating myosin. It is slow but can be sustained. Nitric oxide relaxes it via cGMP.

title: Essential nutrients are those that:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Essential nutrients are those that:
options: Cannot be synthesised by the body
body.explanation: Essential = cannot be synthesised; must come from the diet.

title: Which Ca²⁺-binding regulatory protein is used by smooth muscle?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which Ca²⁺-binding regulatory protein is used by smooth muscle?
body.explanation: Skeletal and cardiac use troponin.

title: Where are the kidneys positioned?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where are the kidneys positioned?
body.explanation: The kidneys are retroperitoneal organs.

title: Which forces oppose filtration? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which forces oppose filtration? (choose all)
body.explanation: Blood colloid osmotic pressure and capsular hydrostatic pressure oppose glomerular hydrostatic pressure.

title: Which taste signals electrolyte balance?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which taste signals electrolyte balance?
body.explanation: Salty signals sodium and osmotic balance; sweet and umami signal energy-rich nutrients; sour and bitter signal acids and possible toxins.

title: What does a positive Babinski sign after age 1.5 mean?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does a positive Babinski sign after age 1.5 mean?
body.explanation: Stroking the lateral sole extends the great toe. Normal under 1.5 years because the corticospinal tract is not yet myelinated; after that it indicates a corticospinal lesion.

title: What is haematuria?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is haematuria?
body.explanation: Proteinuria (albuminuria): protein in urine. Haematuria: blood in urine. Both can follow infection or trauma damaging the filter.

title: Which three events make up the near response?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which three events make up the near response?
body.explanation: Near vision is parasympathetic: the lens thickens, the pupils constrict and the eyes converge.

title: What is tetanus?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is tetanus?
body.explanation: At high frequency the fibre cannot relax between action potentials, so contractions summate. In incomplete tetanus it partly relaxes.

title: Ketones in the urine are called:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Ketones in the urine are called:
body.explanation: Ketones in urine: acetonuria.

title: Micronutrients are:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Micronutrients are:
body.explanation: Only small quantities of vitamins and minerals are needed.

title: Healthy glomerular capillaries are:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Healthy glomerular capillaries are:
options: Lined by podocytes on the blood side
body.explanation: Glomerular capillaries are fenestrated; podocytes line the capsule side.

title: What is meant by all or none?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is meant by all or none?
options: It is always the same size
body.explanation: Once threshold is reached, the action potential has the same magnitude and pattern every time, and spreads without decrement.

title: What is the refractive index of air?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the refractive index of air?
body.explanation: Air's refractive index is 1, and others are calculated relative to it.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
options: Lateral horn (T1 to L2, S2 to S4)
body.explanation: The arrow points to the lateral horn (t1 to l2, s2 to s4).

title: Normal arterial blood pH is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Normal arterial blood pH is:
body.explanation: Systemic arterial blood pH is kept between 7.35 and 7.45.

title: What does the muscle spindle detect?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does the muscle spindle detect?
body.explanation: The spindle signals length; the Golgi tendon organ signals tension.

title: Desirable total cholesterol is below:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Desirable total cholesterol is below:
body.explanation: Desirable below 5.0; high above 6.2 mmol/L.

title: What crosses the synaptic cleft between two neurons?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What crosses the synaptic cleft between two neurons?
options: Ca²⁺ ions from the presynaptic cell
body.explanation: Current cannot flow across the cleft, so a chemical intermediate is needed.

title: Where do pain and temperature fibres cross the midline?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where do pain and temperature fibres cross the midline?
body.explanation: Fine touch and vibration cross in the medulla.

title: Normal urine output per minute is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Normal urine output per minute is about:
body.explanation: 120 filtered − 119 reabsorbed = 1 mL/min (about 1.5 L/day).

title: Ghrelin secretion stops:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Ghrelin secretion stops:
options: Only after a week of fasting
body.explanation: Ghrelin secretion ceases within an hour of eating.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: ATP hydrolysis. ATP is split into ADP + Pi, powering the conformational change.

title: Which types of stimuli does the lecture list as activating neurons? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which types of stimuli does the lecture list as activating neurons? (choose all)
body.explanation: Slide 30: neurons are excitable and are activated by mechanical (touch, vibration, movement), electrical (ion, voltage changes) and chemical (taste, smell, ligands from other cells) stimuli.
option_notes: Listed: taste, smell, ligands from other cells.
Not one of the lecture's stimulus types.

title: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which phase of the action potential is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the resting potential (-70 mv). The fully labelled graph is on the Visual tab.

title: Which diseases can abolish the Achilles reflex? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which diseases can abolish the Achilles reflex? (choose all)
body.explanation: Diabetes, neurosyphilis, alcoholism and subarachnoid haemorrhage can abolish it. Cervical cord compression exaggerates it.

title: Which band contains only thin filaments?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which band contains only thin filaments?
body.explanation: I = isotropic, light.

title: Which protein is missing in Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which protein is missing in Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
body.explanation: An X-linked recessive disorder (Xp21) of dystrophin. Becker dystrophy is milder, with partly functional dystrophin. CK is markedly raised.

title: What is a stressor?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is a stressor?
body.explanation: A stressor challenges the homeostatic state; stress is the physiological or psychological response to it.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Satiety hormones. Leptin, insulin, PYY and CCK inhibit NPY/AgRP neurons.

title: Which are properties of an action potential? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are properties of an action potential? (choose all)
body.explanation: It is all or none, propagates without decrement, keeps the same pattern and travels one way toward the terminal.

title: Why can neurons not divide?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why can neurons not divide?
body.explanation: Neurons have no centrosome, so they have lost the power of division.

title: What does the posterior column carry? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does the posterior column carry? (choose all)
body.explanation: Gracile and cuneate fasciculi: discriminative touch, light pressure, vibration and conscious proprioception. Pain and temperature go in the spinothalamic tract.

title: In the distal convoluted tubule, H+ is secreted by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In the distal convoluted tubule, H+ is secreted by:
body.explanation: Distal H+ secretion uses the hydrogen-ATPase.

title: In the H-reflex recording, which wave comes first?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In the H-reflex recording, which wave comes first?
body.explanation: Stimulating the popliteal fossa first activates motor fibres directly (the M wave), then Ia fibres reach the motor neuron and give the longer-latency H-reflex.

title: Which substances do the kidneys remove from plasma?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which substances do the kidneys remove from plasma?
body.explanation: They remove metabolic wastes, endogenous hormones, exogenous chemicals and free radicals; cells are not filtered.
option_notes: Correct: hormones are cleared from blood.
Wrong: blood cells are not filtered; red cells in urine are abnormal (haematuria).

title: Which two transmitters dominate the analgesia system?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which two transmitters dominate the analgesia system?
body.explanation: PAG fibres secrete enkephalin; raphe fibres secrete serotonin in the dorsal horn, which makes local neurons release enkephalin too.

title: What do most sympathetic postganglionic fibres release?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What do most sympathetic postganglionic fibres release?
body.explanation: NE acts on alpha or beta adrenergic receptors. There are three exceptions.

title: Which nephrons are better at making concentrated urine?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which nephrons are better at making concentrated urine?
body.explanation: Juxtamedullary nephrons have very long loops and maintain the medullary gradient.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Neurotransmitter release. Ca²⁺ causes synaptic vesicles to fuse with the presynaptic membrane and release their transmitter by exocytosis.

title: In myopia, where does light focus?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In myopia, where does light focus?
body.explanation: Myopia: in front of the retina. Hyperopia: behind it. Emmetropia: on it.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the cornea.

title: A triglyceride is made of:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A triglyceride is made of:
options: Glycerol and 2 fatty acids plus phosphate
body.explanation: Glycerol backbone + 3 fatty acids.

title: Which process removes additional wastes from the blood and adds them to the filtrate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which process removes additional wastes from the blood and adds them to the filtrate?
body.explanation: Tubular secretion adds wastes from the blood to the filtrate.

title: How wide is the synaptic cleft at the NMJ?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How wide is the synaptic cleft at the NMJ?
body.explanation: The gap is about 50 nm, and ACh takes about 0.5 ms to diffuse across it.

title: Which glial cells form myelin in the CNS?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which glial cells form myelin in the CNS?
body.explanation: Myelin is formed by oligodendrocytes in the CNS and Schwann cells in the PNS.

title: Which channel type is always open?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which channel type is always open?
body.explanation: Leaky channels are non-gated and always open. The others open in response to voltage, a ligand or physical force.

title: How is the utricular macula oriented with the head upright?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How is the utricular macula oriented with the head upright?
body.explanation: The utricular macula lies horizontally and the saccular macula vertically when the head is upright.

title: What triggers the myotatic reflex?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What triggers the myotatic reflex?
body.explanation: A sudden passive stretch of the muscle belly makes the agonist contract while its antagonist relaxes.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the motor end plate (nicotinic ach receptors). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What does the caloric test stimulate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does the caloric test stimulate?
body.explanation: Warm or cold water in the ear canal appears to stimulate the lateral canal crista directly, producing nystagmus.

title: Where is CSF reabsorbed into the blood?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where is CSF reabsorbed into the blood?
body.explanation: CSF returns to the venous circulation through the arachnoid granulations into the superior sagittal sinus.

title: Through what opening does the singular nerve pass?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Through what opening does the singular nerve pass?
body.explanation: The singular branch to the posterior ampullary crest passes through the foramen singulare.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Nutrients. Ingested chemicals used for growth, repair or maintenance of the body.

title: Which limbic structures respond to psychological stress? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which limbic structures respond to psychological stress? (choose all)
body.explanation: PFC, amygdala, hippocampus, PVN, VTA and nucleus accumbens.

title: Which are functions of the CSF? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are functions of the CSF? (choose all)
body.explanation: Protection, buoyancy, excretion of waste and acting as an endocrine medium for the brain.

title: Which systems are activated in acute stress? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which systems are activated in acute stress? (choose all)
body.explanation: Your professor's question: the SN (plus SAM and HPA) is enhanced; parasympathetic, immune, reproductive and GI activity falls.

title: Cyanide inhibits:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Cyanide inhibits:
body.explanation: Cyanide blocks Complex IV.

title: CCK:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: CCK:
options: Stimulates bile and pancreatic enzyme secretion
body.explanation: GH-RH stimulation is ghrelin's.

title: What happens to blood coagulation in fight or flight?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What happens to blood coagulation in fight or flight?
body.explanation: The coagulation rate rises to minimise blood loss if injury occurs.

title: Where is most filtered bicarbonate reabsorbed?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where is most filtered bicarbonate reabsorbed?
body.explanation: About 85% in the proximal tubule, 10% thick ascending limb, 4.9% distal.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
options: Lateral horn (T1 to L2, S2 to S4)
body.explanation: The arrow points to the white matter (funiculi).

title: How does enkephalin act on the 2nd order neuron?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: How does enkephalin act on the 2nd order neuron?
body.explanation: Enkephalin reduces presynaptic Ca2+ entry and transmitter release, and hyperpolarises the second-order neuron by opening K+ channels.

title: What is kinesthesis?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is kinesthesis?
body.explanation: Kinesthesis, a somatosensory system, tells us the relative position and motion of body parts; it works with equilibrium, mediated by the vestibular system.

title: Why can a single EPSP not fire an action potential?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why can a single EPSP not fire an action potential?
options: It is only about 10 mV, while threshold is 15-20 mV above rest
EPSPs occur only at the axon hillock
body.explanation: -70 to -50/-55 mV needs summation.

title: Why is the optic disc a blind spot?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why is the optic disc a blind spot?
body.explanation: The optic nerve leaves there; the brain fills in the gap using the other eye.

title: Renin converts:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Renin converts:
body.explanation: Renin: angiotensinogen → angiotensin I.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
options: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
Descending limb of the loop of Henle
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Distal convoluted tubule. Selectively secretes and absorbs ions to keep blood pH and electrolytes balanced.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Anabolism. Builds large molecules from small ones; consumes more energy than it releases (endergonic, endothermic).

title: Chylomicrons first enter:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Chylomicrons first enter:
body.explanation: Lymph absorbs chylomicrons from the small intestine, then drains into the blood.

title: ANP:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: ANP:
body.explanation: ANP: afferent dilation, efferent constriction, GFR ↑, natriuresis, renin and aldosterone ↓.
option_notes: Wrong: it dilates the afferent arteriole.

title: Which mechanoreceptor is slowly adapting and in the epidermis?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which mechanoreceptor is slowly adapting and in the epidermis?
body.explanation: Merkel: slowly adapting, about 25%, the only epidermal ones. Meissner: rapidly adapting, about 40%. Pacinian: rapidly adapting, deep, 10 to 15%. Ruffini: slowly adapting, deep.

title: Which enzyme converts H2CO3 to CO2 and water in the tubule?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which enzyme converts H2CO3 to CO2 and water in the tubule?
body.explanation: Carbonic anhydrase.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the utricle.

title: Which arcuate neurons drive hunger?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which arcuate neurons drive hunger?
body.explanation: NPY and AgRP are two potent appetite stimulants.

title: When rotation starts, which way does endolymph tilt the crista?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: When rotation starts, which way does endolymph tilt the crista?
body.explanation: At the start the endolymph lags and tilts the crista opposite to rotation; on stopping it tilts it in the same direction.

title: Which is almost insensitive to pain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is almost insensitive to pain?
body.explanation: The liver parenchyma, the lung alveoli and the brain are almost insensitive to pain.

title: Which chemical may be most responsible for post-injury pain?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which chemical may be most responsible for post-injury pain?
body.explanation: Extracts of damaged tissue cause intense pain, and bradykinin seems the most painful of them.

title: Lactase is also called:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Lactase is also called:
body.explanation: Lactase = β-galactosidase.

title: What causes myasthenia gravis?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What causes myasthenia gravis?
body.explanation: Autoimmune suppression of postsynaptic nicotinic receptors, treated with AChE inhibitors. Lambert-Eaton attacks presynaptic Ca2+ channels.

title: With DNP, oxygen consumption:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: With DNP, oxygen consumption:
body.explanation: Uncoupling increases electron transport and O2 consumption.

title: Ghrelin stimulates the hypothalamus to secrete:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Ghrelin stimulates the hypothalamus to secrete:
body.explanation: Ghrelin stimulates GH-releasing hormone; its receptor is the GH secretagogue receptor.

title: What must happen before a chemical can be tasted?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What must happen before a chemical can be tasted?
body.explanation: It must dissolve in saliva and contact the gustatory hairs; binding then depolarises the taste cell.

title: In established heart disease or diabetes, LDL should be no more than:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In established heart disease or diabetes, LDL should be no more than:
body.explanation: LDL ≤ 2.5 and total cholesterol ≤ 4.5 mmol/L.

title: Which receptor is tonic (slowly adapting)?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which receptor is tonic (slowly adapting)?
options: Touch receptor under a watch strap
body.explanation: Posture needs continuous information.

title: AgRP affects melanocortin signalling by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: AgRP affects melanocortin signalling by:
body.explanation: AgRP inhibits melanocortin secretion/action.

title: Which pH control mechanism is the slowest?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which pH control mechanism is the slowest?
body.explanation: Renal handling of H+/HCO3− is slowest, but the only way to remove non-carbonic acids.

title: A polysaccharide contains:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A polysaccharide contains:
body.explanation: Disaccharide 2, oligosaccharide 3-10, polysaccharide more than 10.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Leptin transport. An abnormal transporter for leptin across the blood-brain barrier blocks the signal.

title: Hans Krebs is known for:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Hans Krebs is known for:
body.explanation: Krebs: the citric acid (Krebs) cycle, Nobel 1953.

title: The final electron acceptor of the electron transport chain is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The final electron acceptor of the electron transport chain is:
body.explanation: Oxygen accepts electrons from cytochrome a3 and protons → water.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the voltage-gated ca2+ channel. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which muscle type has no intrinsic activity?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which muscle type has no intrinsic activity?
body.explanation: Skeletal muscle needs a motor neuron. Smooth muscle has a slow wave and cardiac muscle a pacemaker potential.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Ghrelin. Hunger hormone from the empty stomach; stimulates NPY and AgRP neurons and GH release.

title: What is a delayed, diffuse pain sensation called?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is a delayed, diffuse pain sensation called?
body.explanation: Your professor's own question: second pain, carried by C fibres.

title: Which are macronutrients?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are macronutrients?
body.explanation: Macronutrients: water, carbohydrates, lipids, proteins. Vitamins and minerals are micronutrients.

title: Which is decreased during acute stress?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is decreased during acute stress?
options: Blood flow to the GI tract
body.explanation: Your professor's question: GI blood flow falls, while cardiac output, glucose release, epinephrine and cortisol rise.

title: What does Ca2+ bind to start contraction?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does Ca2+ bind to start contraction?
body.explanation: Ca2+ binds troponin, which shifts tropomyosin and unmasks the myosin-binding sites on actin.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Carbonic anhydrase. Enzyme that speeds the conversion between CO2 + H2O and H2CO3, in tubule cells and the lumen.

title: What separates the parietal and occipital lobes?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What separates the parietal and occipital lobes?
body.explanation: Central sulcus: frontal from parietal. Lateral (Sylvian) fissure: temporal below. Parieto-occipital sulcus: parietal from occipital.

title: Which technique measures brain activity at the molar level?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which technique measures brain activity at the molar level?
body.explanation: Electrophysiology ranges from the molar (EEG) to the cellular (intracellular recording).

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Whole muscle. Attached to bone by tendons; wrapped in epimysium.

title: What does the sympathetic system do to the bronchi?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does the sympathetic system do to the bronchi?
body.explanation: Sympathetic: pupils dilate, bronchi dilate, heart speeds up, gut slows, bladder sphincter contracts. Parasympathetic does the reverse.

title: Which retinal cells produce action potentials?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which retinal cells produce action potentials?
body.explanation: Photoreceptors, bipolar, horizontal and amacrine cells use graded potentials; ganglion cells fire action potentials and form the optic nerve.

body.explanation: 1 000 calories = 1 kcal (physiology) = 1 Calorie (dietetics).

title: What closes the voltage-gated Na+ channel after it opens?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What closes the voltage-gated Na+ channel after it opens?
body.explanation: Na+ channels are closed by a separate inactivation gate. This temporary inactivation also makes the action potential travel only one way.

title: Obesity with high leptin levels suggests:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Obesity with high leptin levels suggests:
options: Leptin deficiency from an ob mutation
body.explanation: High leptin + obesity: abnormal Ob-R.

title: Fat is a better storage form than carbohydrate because it:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Fat is a better storage form than carbohydrate because it:
options: Is easier and faster to digest
Does not need lipoproteins to travel
body.explanation: Hydrophobic and compact, with 9 vs 4 kcal/g.

body.explanation: The arrow points to: Postsynaptic ion channels. Binding opens channels: Na⁺ in gives excitation, Cl⁻ in gives inhibition.

title: Angiotensin II keeps GFR up despite low pressure by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Angiotensin II keeps GFR up despite low pressure by:
body.explanation: It constricts the efferent arteriole, raising glomerular pressure.

title: Which three mechanisms control GFR?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which three mechanisms control GFR?
body.explanation: Renal autoregulation, nervous (sympathetic) control and hormonal control.

title: What does neurophysiology study?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does neurophysiology study?
body.explanation: Neurophysiology studies the functional properties of neurons, glia and networks.

title: Which is an essential amino acid?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which is an essential amino acid?
body.explanation: Essential: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, valine.

title: What does an MLF lesion cause?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What does an MLF lesion cause?
body.explanation: Slowed or absent adduction of the ipsilateral eye with nystagmus of the abducting eye; often from multiple sclerosis.

title: Why are kidneys vulnerable to hypertension?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why are kidneys vulnerable to hypertension?
body.explanation: High glomerular pressure can rupture capillaries, cause nephrosclerosis and renal atherosclerosis, and lead to renal failure.

title: Which are causes of taste impairment? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are causes of taste impairment? (choose all)
body.explanation: Causes include Bell's palsy, oral infections, head trauma, tumours, vitamin deficiencies, wisdom tooth extraction, MS, cancer, radiation, chemotherapy and drugs.

title: Why can't humans digest cellulose?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Why can't humans digest cellulose?
options: It is too large to reach the gut
It is destroyed by stomach acid
body.explanation: Cellulose is non-digestible because humans lack the enzyme.

title: Hexokinase converts glucose into:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Hexokinase converts glucose into:
body.explanation: Hexokinase phosphorylates glucose to G6P, trapping it in the cell.

title: Where is the cell body of the spindle's sensory neuron?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Where is the cell body of the spindle's sensory neuron?
body.explanation: Afferent cell bodies lie in the spinal ganglion of the dorsal root (a T-shaped neuron); efferent cell bodies lie in the ventral horn.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Melanocortin neurons. POMC neurons release α-MSH acting on MC3/MC4 receptors in the paraventricular nucleus to stop eating; leptin stimulates them.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Fluid advances. Repeating pump and advance multiplies the small difference into a steep gradient.

title: After glycolysis, most of glucose's original energy is in:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: After glycolysis, most of glucose's original energy is in:
body.explanation: Most of the energy remains in pyruvate.

title: What happens if GFR is too high?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What happens if GFR is too high?
body.explanation: Fluid flows too fast to reabsorb normally, so urine output rises, risking dehydration and electrolyte loss.

title: Which are causes of muscle fatigue? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which are causes of muscle fatigue? (choose all)
body.explanation: Metabolic depletion, low pH, low glycogen and damage to the sarcolemma and SR. Synaptic fatigue is from lack of ACh.

title: In aerobic respiration, oxygen is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In aerobic respiration, oxygen is:
body.explanation: O2 receives electrons and H2O is produced.

title: Which cells provide lateral inhibition in the retina? (choose all)
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which cells provide lateral inhibition in the retina? (choose all)
body.explanation: Horizontal cells act at the photoreceptor-bipolar level, amacrine cells at the bipolar-ganglion level.

title: What is the direct trigger for neurotransmitter exocytosis?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: What is the direct trigger for neurotransmitter exocytosis?
options: Binding of transmitter to its receptor
body.explanation: Voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels open when the AP arrives.

title: Which afferents are not consciously perceived?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which afferents are not consciously perceived?
body.explanation: From organs of the body cavities.

body.stem: BMI is calculated as:
body.explanation: BMI = W/H².
